messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Stan starts sampling but it freezes
parts:
Hi Siavash,

What version of RStan are you using?

What do you mean by "freeze"? If you looked at your computer's activity, does it actually stop?

You might want to try the stiff solver, integrate_ode_bdf().

You're going to have trouble with the really tight priors you've put down.



Daniel






On Mon, Nov 7, 2016 at 3:31 PM, Siavash Riazi <siar...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello Stan users, 

I'm trying to fit an ODE model using Stan. the model describes growth of a bacterium on methanol and formaldehyde. The model consists of 4 DEs and I'm generating a growth curve using one initial condition and a set of parameters, then using this curve as data to get back parameters I have started with. I have 9 parameters, I define 6 of them with very small standard deviation so they are basically my constants. 3 of them have larger SD and those are what I like to estimate. The program doesn't give any error or warning, when it starts sampling it initialize the chains but then it freeze and never go any further. I would like to know where the issue come from. 

Thanks,     

--

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Stan starts sampling but it freezes
parts:
You need to constrain your parameters to be positive
when they are declared---just applying lognormal won't
make everything behave properly (it'll just cause rejections
and the kinds of messages you see, which can lead to either
bias or just slow sampling).

- Bob
